so is it idiot-proof with regards to the poisonous leaves? i have no experience, but as soon as i saw that, i decided i better not plant it.

@Dumb_Comment_Bot

Leaves are poisonous, stalks are not, it is that simple actually. When you are harvesting just pull off as much as you need of the outermost stalks. Those are obviously the biggest ones too. You can get several harvests in a season if you leave enough for it to keep going and compete with anything else around it (keep 1/2 the leaf surface area, 2/3 of the stalks ish). It'll choke out anything near it as long as it has a head start. The important part of the plant is the root (that's what you plant if you are buying it) so its important not to dig around it and fuck it up. Also to be somewhat gentle as you yank the stalks off.

After a few years it'll get nice and big and you can split it in the fall time if you want to grow more. Dig around it a big and cut off a third or so of the root and transplant that.

There are a few varieties of rhubarb so figure out what goes best in your area/what tastes the best when first getting it. As a rule of thumb the "redder" the stalks the more "rhubarby" it tastes but the greener colored stalks are hardier.
